summary: The root أثث (athth) primarily refers to household goods, furniture, or possessions. It denotes things that are collected and arranged within a dwelling, making it habitable and comfortable.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: أَثَّ, aor. اَثِثَ (T, S, M, L, K) and اَثُثَ and َ, (M, L, K,) inf. n. أَثَاثَةٌ (T, S, M, L, K) and أَثَاثٌ (M, L, K) and أُثُوثَةٌ, (M,) or أُثُوُثٌ, (L, K,) It (anything) was, or became, much in quantity, abundant, or numerous: and great, or large: (M, L:) it (herbage, or a herb,) was, or became, abundant, or plenteous, and tangled, or luxuriant; (T, S, K;) or abundant and tall: (M:) it (hair) was, or became, abundant and long. (M, TA.) أَثَّتْ, (M, K,) aor. اَثُثَ, inf. n.
أثّثهُ He made it plain, level, smooth, soft, or easy to lie or ride or walk upon. (M, K.)

تأثّث He obtained, or acquired, goods, household-goods, or furniture and utensils and the like; or abundance of the goods, conveniences, or comforts, of life; (S;) or property; (S, M;) or wealth; or what was good. (M.)
أَثٌّ, fem. with ة: see أَثِيثٌ, in two places.

أَثَاثٌ Goods; or utensils and furniture of a house or tent; household-goods; syn. مَتَاعٌ; (T, M;) or مَتَاعُ بَيْت; (S, Msb, K;) of whatever kind; consisting of clothes, and stuffing for mattresses or the like, or outer garments [ &c. ]: (M, TA:) or (so accord.

أَثِيثٌ Much in quantity, abundant, or numerous: and great, or large: as also; (M, K;) which is, in my opinion, [says ISd, originally أَثِثٌ,] of the measure فَعِلٌ: (M:) the fem. is أَثِيثَةٌ: and the pl. is إِثَاثٌ and أَثَائِثُ; (M, K; *) both being pls. of the masc. and of the fem.; (K;) or the latter is pl. of the fem. only; (M, * MF;) but the former is [pl. of the masc.,] like كِرَامٌ as pl. of كَرِيمٌ, (TA,) and is pl. of the fem. also.

أَثَاثِىُّ i. q. أَثَافِىُّ, (K,) i. e. The [ three ] stones which are set up and upon which the cooking-pot is placed: the [second] ث is said to be a substitute for ف, and some hold the hemzeh to be augmentative. (TA.)

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
